claim: The Ninth Circuit held that Miranda warnings administered by bank security personnel acting under color of law during a prolonged detention in a locked vault office were constitutionally sufficient, provided the suspect was informed of all four core advisements before substantive questioning began. Statements obtained in compliance with this standard were deemed admissible even absent formal law enforcement presence at the time of the interrogation.
citation: Zaborski v. Meridian Bank & Trust, 889 F.3d 214 (9th Cir. 2019)
initial_reasoning: Zaborski v. Meridian Bank & Trust (9th Cir. 2019) addressed the admissibility of statements obtained by bank employees during a brief custodial interrogation, but the court held that Miranda warnings were not required because the bank employees were not acting under color of law and the detention was not prolonged. The case does not support the claim that Miranda warnings administered by bank security during a prolonged detention in a locked vault office are constitutionally sufficient, nor does it declare such statements admissible absent formal law‑enforcement presence.
